subject: Priority lane request: OEM fulfillment tranche + cloud backfill options
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: OmniOEM Sales <sales@omnioem.com>, Acme AI <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority lane request: OEM fulfillment tranche + cloud backfill options

Hi all,

Quick summary: Acme has signaled a commitment window for Dedicated capacity that begins in Q4 and would like us to guarantee a staggered onramp. They asked for clarity on OEM lead times and whether Redwood can secure an "expedite" lane or staggered tranche delivery + cloud backfill while hardware ships.

Ask to OmniOEM: can you confirm a firm ETA range for the 8x A100/MB4 racks we discussed, whether there is a paid priority lane, and lead time delta if we accept mixed SKUs (e.g., 4x A100 + 4x A40) as an interim? Please attach updated quote breakdown and confirm whether there are allotments we can reserve with a deposit.

Ask to Acme Procurement: we attached a short LOI template (Acme_LOI_draft.pdf) to capture a carveout/commitment signal if needed. Are you able to sign a non-binding LOI by next Tue (2027-07-06)? That gives us room to negotiate priority with OmniOEM and push a limited reservation to GCP as a cloud backstop.

Internal notes for Karthik/Ben/Laura: please see the proposed fallback plan below — we need a quick decision on how far we want to push cash deposit vs. cloud reserve credits. I propose:
- Tranche A (Q4 start): reserve 50% of units via OEM priority lane (deposit-based), accept mixed SKUs for 4 weeks as warm-up.
- Tranche B (Q1 ramp): remaining units delivered as standard OEM schedule; reserve cloud burst credits to cover 2 months of peak.

I'll coordinate pricing/legal once OmniOEM returns the updated quote.

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Dedicated Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: OmniOEM Sales <sales@omnioem.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Acme AI <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Oliver Tran <oliver.tran@omnioem.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority lane request: OEM fulfillment tranche + cloud backfill options

Kimberly / Acme team —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front:
1) ETA for 8 racks (A100 MB4 spec) on standard queue: 16-22 weeks from PO.
2) Priority lane (paid expedite): we can move that to 8-10 weeks from PO with a 20% expedite premium and a 30% refundable deposit to secure the production slot.
3) Mixed SKU option: yes, we can allocate mixed SKUs (A100/A40) with a 10% per-unit delta in performance guarantees; lead time shortens by ~4 weeks on average because A40 components are more available.

Attached: omnioem_quoteline_v2.xlsx (quote lines + expedite pricing).

A couple of operational notes: we can hold a partial reservation for 30 days after deposit; after that the slot moves to standard queue. If Redwood wants multi-tranche delivery, we can split the PO into two shipments with staggered manufacturing slots — deposit covers the first tranche.

If you want we can issue a formal reservation agreement (1-2 page) the same day we receive a signed LOI or deposit instruction.

Best,
Sophie Nguyen
Strategic Accounts — OmniOEM

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority lane request: OEM fulfillment tranche + cloud backfill options

Kim / team —

Thanks, OmniOEM — good context. A few operational clarifications from infra/procurement side:
- We should avoid a full cash outlay if possible; prefer a refundable deposit structure tied to a short SLA (e.g., invoice + release if not shipped within X weeks).
- Mixed-SKU bridge: acceptable as long as we guarantee consistent inference latency envelope for customer SLAs. Ops will need to validate performance for A40 warm-up nodes; suggest a 2-week soak test window in our staging pool before handing to Acme.
- Cloud backstop: recommend reserving GCP committed use discounts for the tranche duration rather than on-demand credits — better for predictability and cheaper overall. Ben, can you run a quick cost delta (3 months) vs a deposit hold?

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to request a simple reservation agreement from OmniOEM (1 page).
2) Acme to sign LOI by Tue 7/6 if they can; LOI triggers deposit instruction.
3) Ben to deliver cost delta by EOD 7/5 so we can finalize recommendation to leadership.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Partnerships

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority lane request: OEM fulfillment tranche + cloud backfill options

Quick cost snapshot (high level) — see attached (gcp_reserved_report_June2027.pdf) for regional pricing assumptions.
- 8 rack OEM expedite deposit (30% of list price) = ~$480k deposit; expedite premium ~20% increases unit cost by ~$320k over standard schedule.
- GCP 3-month reserved capacity to cover equivalent peak: estimated $210k (includes network + storage egress buffer).
- Delta to use OEM expedite vs cloud-reserve backfill (3 month overlap): ~$100k higher for expedite, but expedite shortens delivery by ~8-12 weeks which materially reduces risk of SLA misses and revenue delay for the Acme deal.

Recommendation: hybrid approach. Secure a smaller OEM deposit to hold the production slot for Tranche A (cover 50% units), backstop the remainder with GCP reserved credits for 3 months; once OEM units arrive, cancel portion of the cloud reservations. That keeps cash tied up lower and gives us guaranteed slot behavior.

Will prepare an exec summary slide for leadership approval if we decide to proceed.

-Ben
Head of Capacity Finance

From: Acme AI <procurement@acme.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, OmniOEM Sales <sales@omnioem.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@acme.ai>
Bcc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority lane request: OEM fulfillment tranche + cloud backfill options

Hi Kimberly / Sophie —

Appreciate the transparency. Acme is prepared to sign the non-binding LOI (we attached a few minor redlines to the payment language) and commit to the expedited tranche for Tranche A, conditional on Redwood executing the reservation agreement with OmniOEM and keeping sight of the refundable deposit clause. We expect our procurement committee to sign the LOI by EOD Wed 7/7, contingent on the reservation agreement draft.

Action items we need from Redwood today:
- Reservation agreement draft from OmniOEM (or their attorney) for internal review.
- Confirmation of the precise deposit amount and refund trigger windows.

Sophie — can your team confirm the reservation agreement timeline? If we can get the one-page agreement before close of business Wed, we can meet Acme's internal sign-off window.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Procurement Manager — Acme AI
